findings.summary: `setInterval(...)` on the return value is never assigned to `pingTimer` (declared empty on the line above), so `pingTimer` stays `undefined` for the lifetime of that `connect()` call. The teardown call `clearInterval(pingTimer)` in `ws.onclose` (line 876) therefore calls `clearInterval(undefined)`, a no-op — the old interval is never actually cancelled. This is the exact failure mode the brief called out by name: 'make sure the ping timer from a previous connection is torn down when the socket closes, so reconnecting doesn't leave multiple ping loops running concurrently.' As written, every reconnect (each dropped/re-established WS) spawns a brand-new 15s ping loop that lives forever; after N reconnects there are N concurrent setInterval loops each independently sending 'ping' every 15s. Fix is a one-token change: `pingTimer=setInterval(function(){...`.
